blocks.text: A 9-year-old girl has had a persistent fungal infection of her mouth and nails since toddlerhood. Her adrenal glands then fail and she has convulsions caused by low blood calcium from hypoparathyroidism. She has inherited a defect in one transcription factor in the thymus, and the result is an immune system that attacks her own endocrine organs.

blocks.markdown: The lymphocyte antigen receptors are produced by random gene rearrangement, so some inevitably recognise self. **Immune tolerance** is the set of mechanisms that prevents these cells from causing damage. Tolerance is divided by where it happens: **central tolerance** in the primary lymphoid organs (thymus for T cells, bone marrow for B cells) and **peripheral tolerance** in the tissues and lymph nodes.

blocks.title: Immune tolerance
blocks.text: Unresponsiveness of the immune system to an antigen. Tolerance to self antigens (self-tolerance) is learned during lymphocyte development and maintained in the periphery; failure produces autoimmunity.

blocks.markdown: **Central tolerance.** In the thymus, developing T cells whose receptors bind self peptide-MHC with **high** affinity are eliminated by **negative selection** (clonal deletion, apoptosis). Some self-reactive CD4⁺ cells are diverted into the regulatory T cell lineage instead. In the bone marrow, immature B cells whose receptors bind self antigen strongly may undergo **receptor editing** (rearrangement of a new light chain) or are deleted. Central tolerance cannot be complete, because a T cell can only be tested against antigens present in the thymus.

**AIRE.** The **autoimmune regulator (AIRE)** is a transcription factor expressed by **medullary thymic epithelial cells**. It switches on the ectopic expression of many **tissue-restricted antigens** (for example insulin, thyroglobulin and proteins of other endocrine organs) that would normally be found only in their own tissues. Thymocytes that react to these antigens are deleted or diverted into the regulatory T cell lineage. Without AIRE, self-reactive T cells escape the thymus and cause organ-specific autoimmunity. Biallelic AIRE mutation causes **APECED** (autoimmune polyendocrinopathy-candidiasis-ectodermal dystrophy, also called autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 1), an autosomal recessive disease with chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, hypoparathyroidism and adrenal insufficiency.

blocks.title: Why do these organs fail?
blocks.prompt: A child has a homozygous loss-of-function AIRE mutation. Explain why autoimmune attack occurs against the parathyroid and adrenal glands specifically.

steps.text: Recall AIRE's role. It drives expression of tissue-restricted antigens in medullary thymic epithelial cells.
Without AIRE, the parathyroid and adrenal antigens are not displayed in the thymus, so T cells (and Treg precursors) specific for them are not removed or diverted.
These autoreactive T cells emigrate to the periphery. Peripheral tolerance is incomplete, and when they meet their antigen in the endocrine organs, attack occurs.
The pattern is organ-specific, multi-endocrine autoimmunity, with antibodies against affected organs.

blocks.answer: Loss of AIRE removes thymic display of tissue-restricted antigens, so tissue-specific T cells escape and attack endocrine glands.

blocks.markdown:
**Peripheral tolerance** deals with self-reactive cells that escaped central tolerance or recognise antigens never present in the thymus. The main mechanisms are:

- **Anergy:** a lymphocyte that recognises antigen without co-stimulation (signal 1 without signal 2 via CD28-B7) becomes functionally unresponsive. This commonly happens when a self antigen is presented by APCs that have not been activated by danger signals.
- **Regulatory T cells (Tregs):** CD4⁺ CD25⁺ FOXP3⁺ cells suppress other lymphocytes by IL-10, TGF-β, IL-2 consumption and CTLA-4.
- **Deletion:** repeated stimulation causes **activation-induced cell death** via Fas-Fas ligand.
- **Immune privilege:** sites such as the eye and testis restrict immune access.
- **Ignorance:** some antigens are simply sequestered or at low concentration.

rows: Negative selection (deletion), receptor editing, Treg generation; AIRE
Anergy, Tregs, activation-induced cell death, immune privilege
Those present in thymus/marrow, including AIRE-driven tissue antigens
Antigens that were not present centrally or cells that escaped
Autoimmunity when stimulated, e.g. FOXP3 loss in IPEX

Number of thymocytes exiting equals those made multiplied by the surviving fraction

blocks.title: Counting what escapes
blocks.prompt: In a model, 5.0 × 10^7 thymocytes arrive in the thymus per day and only 2% survive selection. Estimate how many mature T cells exit per day, and explain why this fraction is small.

steps.text: Convert the percentage into a fraction.

Interpretation: most thymocytes are lost, either because their TCR cannot recognise self MHC (death by neglect) or because it binds self too strongly (negative selection). The quoted 2% is a model figure for illustration.

blocks.answer: 1.0 × 10^6 cells per day, with most thymocytes eliminated by selection.

blocks.title: Anergy needs no co-stimulation
blocks.text: A naive T cell that sees a self peptide on an APC without co-stimulatory B7 signals does not activate; it is rendered anergic. Co-stimulation appears only after danger signals, so normal tissue antigens do not trigger attack.

blocks.title: Tolerance is a balance
blocks.text: Tolerance can be broken by infection (inflammation raising co-stimulation), tissue injury releasing sequestered antigens, or genetic defects in AIRE, FOXP3 or CTLA-4.

points: Central tolerance removes strongly self-reactive T cells (negative selection) and B cells (editing, deletion) in the thymus and bone marrow.
AIRE in medullary thymic epithelial cells displays tissue-restricted antigens; AIRE loss causes APECED.
Peripheral tolerance uses anergy, regulatory T cells, deletion and immune privilege.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes central from peripheral tolerance?

options.text: Central tolerance acts in the thymus and bone marrow on developing lymphocytes
Peripheral tolerance acts only in the thymus
Central tolerance acts only on mature T cells in tissues
Peripheral tolerance eliminates cells before they express receptors

questions.correctOptionText: Central tolerance acts in the thymus and bone marrow on developing lymphocytes

distractorRationale.a: Correct: central tolerance happens during development in primary lymphoid organs.
distractorRationale.b: Peripheral tolerance acts outside primary lymphoid organs.
distractorRationale.c: Central tolerance acts on developing, not mature, cells.
distractorRationale.d: Peripheral tolerance acts on mature lymphocytes that express receptors.

questions.explanation: Central tolerance operates in the thymus (T cells) and bone marrow (B cells) as lymphocytes develop, whereas peripheral tolerance controls mature lymphocytes in lymph nodes and tissues.

questions.stem: An immature B cell in the bone marrow strongly binds a membrane self antigen. Which outcome is possible?

options.text: Receptor editing by rearranging a new light chain

questions.correctOptionText: Receptor editing by rearranging a new light chain

distractorRationale.a: Correct: editing can replace the self-reactive light chain; if it fails the cell is deleted.
distractorRationale.b: Plasma cells arise after activation in the periphery.
distractorRationale.c: Class switching requires T cell help later.
distractorRationale.d: Germinal centre entry follows activation in lymph nodes.

questions.explanation: Immature B cells with self-reactive receptors can edit their light-chain genes to change specificity, or undergo apoptosis. This is central B cell tolerance.

questions.stem: AIRE promotes tolerance mainly by which mechanism?

options.text: Inducing thymic epithelial expression of tissue-restricted self antigens so that reactive T cells are deleted
Suppressing MHC class I in the thymus

questions.correctOptionText: Inducing thymic epithelial expression of tissue-restricted self antigens so that reactive T cells are deleted

distractorRationale.a: Correct: AIRE drives ectopic expression of tissue-specific antigens.
distractorRationale.b: AIRE does not suppress MHC class I expression.
distractorRationale.c: AIRE is not a complement regulator.
distractorRationale.d: AIRE is not involved in class switching.

questions.explanation: AIRE in medullary thymic epithelial cells causes display of antigens usually restricted to peripheral organs, so that T cells reactive to them are deleted or diverted into Tregs.

questions.stem: A T cell encounters a self peptide-MHC complex on a resting APC lacking B7 molecules. Which fate is most likely?

distractorRationale.a: Correct: signal 1 without CD28 co-stimulation causes anergy.
distractorRationale.b: Th17 differentiation needs co-stimulation and polarising cytokines.
distractorRationale.d: T cells do not become plasma cells.

questions.explanation: Without co-stimulation the T cell becomes anergic. This peripheral tolerance mechanism stops responses to self antigens presented outside inflammation.

questions.stem: A boy has early-onset severe autoimmune enteropathy, type 1 diabetes and eczema, due to a mutation in a transcription factor expressed in CD4⁺ CD25⁺ cells. What is the most likely mechanism?

options.text: Absence of functioning regulatory T cells

questions.correctOptionText: Absence of functioning regulatory T cells

distractorRationale.a: Correct: FOXP3 mutation (IPEX) abolishes Treg function and causes multi-organ autoimmunity.
distractorRationale.b: T cell receptor absence would cause immunodeficiency, not autoimmunity.
distractorRationale.c: Class switching defects do not cause this syndrome.
distractorRationale.d: A burst defect causes infection, not autoimmunity.

questions.explanation: FOXP3 is the master transcription factor of regulatory T cells. Its loss causes IPEX, where unrestrained effector T cells attack multiple organs, illustrating the role of Tregs in peripheral tolerance.

questions.stem: True or false: negative selection removes thymocytes whose receptors bind self peptide-MHC with high affinity.
questions.explanation: Thymocytes with high-affinity self-reactive TCRs undergo apoptosis (negative selection) or are diverted into the Treg lineage. This is central T cell tolerance.

questions.stem: In a mouse model, 6.0 × 10^7 thymocytes enter selection per day and 3% survive to leave the thymus. How many leave per day (in units of 10^5 cells)?
questions.explanation: The number leaving = 6.0 × 10^7 × 0.03 = 18 × 10^5. The figure illustrates that most thymocytes do not survive selection.

questions.stem: APECED is autosomal recessive. Two carrier parents have an unaffected child. What is the probability, in percent, that this unaffected child is a carrier?
questions.explanation: Among children of two carriers, the genotypes are 1/4 unaffected non-carrier, 1/2 carrier, 1/4 affected. Given the child is unaffected, the probability of being a carrier is (1/2)/(3/4) = 2/3, or 66.7%.

questions.stem: Describe how AIRE contributes to thymic tolerance and what happens in AIRE deficiency.
markingGuide: AIRE is a transcription factor in medullary thymic epithelial cells
Induces expression of tissue-restricted antigens in the thymus
Self-reactive T cells deleted (negative selection) or diverted to Tregs
In deficiency, reactive T cells escape and cause organ-specific autoimmunity
APECED: candidiasis, hypoparathyroidism, adrenal failure; autosomal recessive
questions.explanation: AIRE extends the range of self antigens the thymus can test, so its failure leaves tissue-specific T cells.

questions.stem: Explain how anergy and regulatory T cells maintain peripheral tolerance.
markingGuide: Anergy: antigen recognition without co-stimulation (no CD28/B7) causes functional inactivation
Co-stimulation is expressed only on activated APCs, so self antigens usually lack it
They suppress via IL-10, TGF-β, IL-2 consumption and CTLA-4
Loss of Tregs (FOXP3 mutation) causes autoimmunity
questions.explanation: The two mechanisms operate in tissues to silence or suppress self-reactive lymphocytes that escaped deletion.
